newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas centred on prompt, but busy through 1999.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas centred on prompt, but busy through 1999.

text.p: The U.K. physical natural gas market was actively traded across several periods on Tuesday, with the market particularly busy in the very prompt period, in the fourth quarter of this year and, unusually, in 1999.

One large player was responsible for buying big volumes of gas on the within day and day ahead markets. The same buyer had been active on Monday for the same periods, although prices on the within-day market were lower than they were the previous day.
There were persistent rumours of production or maintenance problems leading the buyer to need such large volumes of short term gas.

But the buyer played them down, and exact details of what caused the prompt interest were hard to obtain. Some said that an extension to a planned maintenance was behind the demand, but this was not confirmed.
There was also a spate of interest in gas in the fourth quarter, with several trades done in a tight range between 13.30 pence and 13.35 pence a therm.
"It's all still within the same ranges," said a trader, who added that the lack of price volatility over the last few weeks had deterred traders from taking positions recently.

There was also trade seen next summer, and two separate strips done for the first three quarters of 1999. One of these was done as a strip and one was done with the three quarters traded separately, but this was also in effect a strip at the same price as the other one.

It is thought that no trade has yet been done as far forward as the year 2000, but traders now expect it to happen soon, and several dealers are apparently keen to be the first to strike a deal in the new millennium.

While the physical market was far more active than it has been recently, IPE futures remained quiet and dull, with only 110 lots done as well as two Exchanges for Physical of 100 lots each. IPE brokers are also citing the lack of volatility as a deterrent factor to trading the contract.
